accepted.title: Kawacatoose First Nation members head south to retrieve stolen teepee cover from U.S. | CBC News
propositions: After a century-long absence, a stolen teepee cover will at last be returned to its rightful owners and their community in Saskatchewan.
Kawacatoose First Nation Chief Cory (Okimow) Dustyhorn consulted with the Smithsonian Institution to secure the beautiful cover his great-great-grandfather spent two years crafting.
Now, he and a few of his family members, alongside First Nations University of Canada Indigenous studies professor Andrew Miller, are making the 29-hour drive to Washington, D.C. to retrieve it.
"We started off with a pipe ceremony," Dustyhorn told CBC News.
"I went to a respected elder, and asked for a clear road ahead for us."
When they first began trying to get the cover back, he never imagined the day would finally arrive, he said.

accepted.title: FoN declares zero tolerance for mining in the ocean | Ghana News Agency
propositions: Ghana's preferred news source: Accurate, Credible, Objective, Timely Dixcove (W/R), Oct.

08, GNA – Friends of the Nation (FoN), a non-government organisation (NGO), has declared zero tolerance for mining activities in the ocean as part of its efforts to ensure justice in fisheries governance.

The declaration followed government’s proposed offshore gold reconnaissance deal, granting 10 contiguous offshore reconnaissance licences to Gold Coast Resources Ghana Limited to undertake gold mining in Ghana’s marine waters from Half-Assini in Jomoro to Winneba in the Effutu Municipality in the Western and Central Regions.
According to the NGO, gold mining in the high seas would disrupt the activities of artisanal fishers, thereby bringing fishing expeditions to a standstill.
Mr Mevuta Donkris, the Executive Director of the FoN, said this at a day’s workshop for stakeholders in the fishing industry at Dixcove in the Ahanta West Municipality of the Western Region.

It was organised by FoN under the project dubbed “Protecting Our Zone, Securing Our Future” and was attended by chief fishermen and women from Lower and Upper Dixcove, canoe owners, fish mongers, fishers, the Fisheries Commission, FoN and the media.

accepted.title: Minerals Commission suspends reconnaissance license of Gold Coast GRC Ghana Limited - MyJoyOnline
propositions: The Minerals Commission has suspended the Reconnaissance License of Gold Coast GRC Ghana Limited.
A letter intercepted by Myjoyonline indicates that the decision to suspend the license is part of the mining sector clean-up being carried out by the regulator.

Minister for Lands and Natural Resources has directed the immediate suspension of all activities being undertaken under the licences." It said, "The suspension shall remain in effect until the Commission has completed the necessary consultations and issued the requisite written Ministerial authorisation for the resumption of activities.

During this period, the company is required to cooperate fully with the Commission, other relevant State institutions and all affected stakeholders in addressing the concerns raised and ensuring that all applicable regulatory, environmental and social requirements are duly satisfied.
